completion_reason: Material validation and safety decisions remain around corrupted evidence, cancellation truthfulness, and production provider certification.

questions.label: Corrupted run evidence
questions.context: An evidence-integrity failure means a required artifact is missing, unreadable, or no longer matches its recorded hash. This can make a run’s validation or approval record unreliable even if its status says completed.
questions.evidence: `services/nexus-node/src/run-coordinator.mjs` returns canonical run, result, experiment, and artifact records, while `adapters/runtime-adapters/src/sqlite-store.mjs` persists snapshots and events in SQLite WAL. Together they form the record used to justify approvals and workspace promotion.
questions.impact: This determines whether approvals, promotion, replay, and artifact access remain trustworthy after storage corruption. Long term, it defines whether NexusCentral is an evidence authority or merely a best-effort activity log.
questions.question: What must NexusCentral do when required evidence for a run is missing or fails its integrity check?

choices.consequence: Immediately block approval, promotion, and evidence-dependent replay; preserve the run as quarantined until repair and explicit revalidation succeed. This reduces availability but provides a durable fail-closed trust model.

Rebuild evidence from surviving events and artifacts, then resume automatically when reconstructed hashes agree. This improves recovery speed but makes automated repair part of the trusted validation boundary.
Display the integrity failure but permit a human to approve or promote anyway. This keeps work moving but permanently weakens the meaning of immutable evidence.

questions.recommendation_reason: Approvals and source-workspace promotion should never rely on evidence NexusCentral cannot verify; quarantine preserves forensic history while making recovery explicit.

questions.label: Harness cancellation truth
questions.context: Confirmed cancellation means NexusCentral has evidence that the external harness process stopped and cannot continue writing artifacts or workspace changes. A cancellation request alone does not prove termination.
questions.evidence: `packages/contracts/index.mjs` currently includes a terminal `canceled` run state; `kits/jobs-kit/index.mjs` owns cancellation and timeout; `adapters/runtime-adapters/src/harness-executors.mjs` launches direct-inference and Codex CLI work. `docs/12-IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS.md` lists interrupted harness replay as unproven.
questions.impact: This changes the run state machine and what the Runs tab may truthfully report during uncertain termination. Long term, it prevents hidden background work and unsafe reuse of a SimSpace after cancellation.
questions.question: When may an externally executed harness run enter the terminal canceled state?

choices.consequence: Keep the run nonterminal with cancellation requested until the executor confirms termination; if confirmation is lost, mark it recovery-required or failed and quarantine its workspace. This is slower but keeps state truthful and safe.
Mark canceled once the executor accepts the request, while quarantining outputs until process cleanup completes. This is more responsive but treats acknowledgment as sufficient evidence.
Mark canceled as soon as the operator clicks cancel and clean up asynchronously. This gives the fastest UX but can conceal continued execution or late workspace writes.

questions.recommendation_reason: A terminal state should describe proven reality; requiring termination evidence prevents NexusCentral from presenting an unsafe or still-running harness as finished.

questions.label: Provider production proof
questions.context: Provider certification means the evidence required before a provider and model may be selected for ordinary production routing without an experimental warning. It is separate from runtime eligibility checks such as heart
questions.evidence: `packages/contracts/index.mjs` defines presets for OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Google, Azure, and AWS Bedrock protocols. `docs/12-IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS.md` records live LM Studio proof but only contract-level cloud proof because real cloud credentials have not been tested.
questions.impact: This decides which advertised integrations production workflows may actually depend on at launch. Long term, it establishes a repeatable certification ledger as providers, models, and protocol versions change.
questions.question: What proof should be required before a provider family is available for default production routing?

choices.consequence: Permit production routing only for provider, adapter, and model combinations that pass live authenticated capability, streaming, timeout, and failure tests; keep other presets visible but experimental and excluded by default. This narrows initial availability while creating strong, scalable release证

Allow any preset that passes mocked and contract tests, with warnings for combinations lacking live credential proof. This broadens launch support but moves integration failures into operator workflows.

Remove unproven cloud families from the production UI and API until live validation is completed. This is clearest for operators but narrows the documented architecture and increases later reintroduction work.

questions.recommendation_reason: Tiered live certification preserves the existing multi-provider architecture without representing untested credentialed integrations as production-ready.
